items.headline: PM Wong meets Putin at the ASEAN-Russia summit in Kazan
items.summary: PM Lawrence Wong met Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the ASEAN-Russia Commemorative Summit in Kazan on June 18, his first trip to Russia since Singapore sanctioned Moscow over Ukraine in 2022; Putin said sanctions had held back economic ties.

items.headline: PM Wong and Erdogan agree to deepen ties in Istanbul talks
items.summary: On his way home from Kazan, PM Wong met Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Istanbul on June 19; the two agreed to strengthen cooperation in defence, aviation, maritime affairs and finance.

items.headline: Singapore enters its dengue peak season as weekly cases hit a 2026 high
items.summary: Singapore is in its annual dengue peak season, with the NEA reporting the highest weekly case count of the year so far and several red-alert clusters; residents in northern estates were urged to clear stagnant water.

items.headline: Singapore households can claim $500 in CDC vouchers brought forward to June
items.summary: A $500 CDC Vouchers package, split equally between heartland merchants and supermarkets, became claimable this month after the government brought the disbursement forward to ease living costs; officials warned that SMS claim links are scams.

items.headline: NEET-UG re-exam goes ahead for 22.79 lakh candidates under tight security
items.summary: The NEET-UG re-examination was held on June 21 (2pm-5.15pm) for about 22.79 lakh candidates across roughly 5,400 centres in 565 cities after the May 3 paper was scrapped over a leak; the Indian Air Force ferried question papers under heavy security.

items.headline: Amit Shah reviews security for the Amarnath Yatra starting July 3
items.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah chaired a high-level meeting on the 52-day Amarnath Yatra beginning July 3; about 670 companies of security forces are being deployed, with a new Army Vikas Battalion guarding heights on the Pahalgam route for the first time.

items.headline: Monsoon set to miss Delhi's normal June 27 onset as Mumbai gets a yellow alert
items.summary: The IMD said the southwest monsoon is unlikely to reach Delhi by its usual June 27 onset date as pre-monsoon heat persists, while Mumbai was placed under a yellow alert for thunderstorms on June 22-23 as moisture builds over the Arabian Sea.

items.headline: Update: Iran declares the Strait of Hormuz closed over Israel's strikes in Lebanon
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on June 20 that the Strait of Hormuz was closed in response to Israeli strikes on Hezbollah in Lebanon, straining the days-old interim US-Iran deal; US Central Command said commercial traffic actually rose, and implementation talks were set for Switzerland on June 21.

items.headline: Brazil beat Haiti 3-0 as Cunha scores twice at the World Cup
items.summary: Matheus Cunha scored twice and Vinicius Junior added a third as Brazil beat Haiti 3-0 in Philadelphia on June 20, recovering from their opening draw with Morocco to top Group C.

items.headline: United States beat Australia 2-0 to reach the World Cup knockout round
items.summary: The US beat Australia 2-0 in Seattle on June 19 through a Cameron Burgess own goal and an Alex Freeman header to clinch a round-of-32 spot with a game to spare, their first back-to-back World Cup wins since 1930, despite missing the injured Christian Pulisic.

items.headline: Trump urges the EU to hit China and India with steep tariffs over Russia
items.summary: President Donald Trump has urged the EU to impose tariffs of up to 100% on China and India to pressure Moscow over Ukraine, Reuters reported, citing the Financial Times, signalling fresh friction between Washington and Brussels.

items.headline: Manus's early backers reportedly plan a $2 billion buyback from Meta
items.summary: The early investors in AI-agent startup Manus are reportedly preparing to buy it back from Meta at roughly the $2 billion valuation Meta paid, after Beijing ordered the December deal unwound on national-security grounds, according to The Information; backers said to be involved include HSG, Tencent and ZhenFund.

items.headline: Oil rises on Friday but ends the week down about 8% as the Iran truce holds
items.summary: Brent crude rose 0.9% to $80.57 a barrel on June 19 and WTI added about 1.2% to $77.54 after US-Iran talks in Switzerland were abruptly postponed, but both benchmarks still fell roughly 8% on the week as Hormuz shipping recovered.

items.headline: Asian markets end Friday mixed with US markets shut for Juneteenth
items.summary: Asian equities closed mixed on June 19, with Japan's Nikkei 225 up about 0.3% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng down around 1.6%; US markets were closed for the Juneteenth holiday.

items.headline: Indian rupee logs its best week in about 11 weeks on foreign inflows
items.summary: The Indian rupee posted its strongest weekly performance in around 11 weeks, supported by a surge of foreign investment, even as benchmark indices slipped on Friday in an IT-led selloff after Accenture's weak outlook.

items.headline: Pegula beats Sabalenka to reach the Berlin Open final
items.summary: Defending champion Jessica Pegula rallied past world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka 6-2, 6-7(4), 6-0 to reach the Berlin grass-court final, her fourth career win over Sabalenka.

items.headline: Noskova ends Eala's run to set up a Berlin final with Pegula
items.summary: Eighth seed Linda Noskova beat wild card Alexandra Eala 6-2, 6-4 to reach her first Berlin final, ending Eala's breakout grass-court run; she meets Jessica Pegula for the title.

items.headline: Fritz beats Zverev again to reach the Halle Open final
items.summary: Taylor Fritz beat top seed Alexander Zverev 6-7(4), 6-4, 7-5 in Halle for his seventh straight win over the German, ending Zverev's winning streak and reaching his first final there.

items.headline: Tiafoe routs Altmaier to set up an all-American Halle final
items.summary: Frances Tiafoe beat Germany's Daniel Altmaier 6-1, 6-3 in just over an hour to reach the Halle final, where he faces compatriot Taylor Fritz in their first meeting on grass.

items.headline: India sweep Afghanistan 3-0 as Jaiswal hits a century
items.summary: Yashasvi Jaiswal struck an unbeaten century and Prasidh Krishna took 5/23 as India beat Afghanistan by nine wickets in the third ODI in Chennai on June 20 to complete a 3-0 sweep; Shubman Gill was named player of the series.

items.headline: Australia thrash the Netherlands by 98 runs at the Women's T20 World Cup
items.summary: Australia kept up their unbeaten Women's T20 World Cup run with a 98-run win over the Netherlands in Southampton on June 20, tightening their grip on top spot in Group 1.

fun_fact.headline: The shortest war in history lasted under 45 minutes
fun_fact.body: The shortest war in recorded history lasted well under an hour. On 27 August 1896, a dispute over the throne of Zanzibar led British warships to open fire on the Sultan's palace at around 9am; the Sultan's forces surrendered roughly 38 minutes later. Historians put the whole Anglo-Zanzibar War at somewhere between 38 and 45 minutes.

puzzle.title: One Question, Two Guards
puzzle.body: You reach a fork in the road. One path leads to freedom, the other to certain doom, but you do not know which is which. Two guards stand at the fork: one always tells the truth, the other always lies, and you cannot tell them apart. You may ask only ONE yes/no question, to ONE of the guards, then you must choose a path. What single question guarantees you pick the path to freedom?
puzzle.approach: You cannot trust either answer on its own, so design a question whose answer is routed through both guards, cancelling the lie.
puzzle.answer: Ask either guard: 'If I asked the OTHER guard whether the left path leads to freedom, would he say yes?' Then take the OPPOSITE of the answer. Asking the truth-teller, he honestly reports the liar's false answer; asking the liar, he falsely reports the truth-teller's true answer, so the reply is always the reverse of the truth. If he says yes, take the right path; if he says no, take the left.
